uncited: Coordinate System and Parametric Intersection provides the geometric primitives for determining ray intersections within structured voxel grids, specifically spherical coordinate systems, and for computing approximate intersections with complex volumetric structures like caustic beams.

It solves the problem of efficiently traversing and testing rays against non-Cartesian boundaries (azimuthal and polar sections) and approximating intersections with curved volumetric primitives where exact methods are computationally prohibitive.

It is distinguished from sibling methods like [Ray-Tetrahedron Intersection](2525-ray-tetrahedron-intersection.md) by its specific handling of spherical grid topology and from [Exact Rational Ray-Surfel Evaluation](2915-exact-rational-ray-surfel-evaluation.md) by its reliance on angular decomposition and scan-plane approximations.
The family relies on decomposing complex 3D intersection tests into 2D geometric operations within specific coordinate planes.
For spherical grids, the azimuthal and polar intersections are computed by projecting the ray and voxel boundaries onto the XZ and XY planes, respectively.
The core mechanism involves calculating 2D cross products (determinants) to determine the relative orientation of the ray vector against the voxel boundary vectors.
These perpendicular components are then passed to a generalized `angularHit` function, which handles the logic for entry, exit, and collinearity.

For parametric approximations, the method transforms ray data into local coordinate spaces and uses auxiliary geometric constructs (scan planes) to reduce curved surface intersections to planar triangle tests.
An approximate method to determine if a camera ray intersects a caustic beam and the location of that intersection, used because exact computation is too costly for thousands of beams.

The spherical coordinate intersection methods (Azimuthal and Polar) are part of the infrastructure for spherical voxel grid traversal, often used in global illumination and caustic rendering where spherical symmetry or specific grid structures are advantageous.

The Ray-Ray intersection method is a standard technique in computer graphics for finding the closest approach between skew lines, frequently used in ray tracing acceleration structures and multi-view geometry.
